chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from Hammad ibn Muhammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) over the deceased is five Takbirs."

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), a key component of the funeral prayer.
key_terms.خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: Five Takbirations, referring to the specific count of divine glorifications in the ritual.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirations are recited in the Shia funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the predominant Shia view that the funeral prayer consists of exactly five Takbirations, a practice rooted in the traditions of Imam al-Sadiq (AS). While some early scholars debated the number, this narration solidifies the five-Takbir format as the standard ritual act of worship for the deceased, emphasizing the continuity of prophetic tradition through the Ahl al-Bayt. The act serves as a communal obligation (or recommended individual duty depending on the school) to honor the departed and seek divine mercy for their soul.
